ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p296/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p296/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p296/r4.claim: Favours and deprivation test whether people become grateful and fulfill others' rights or grow conceited, and whether they remain content or despair; the peaceful soul succeeds.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p296/r4.anchor: He is testing whether blessing someone with favours makes him grateful

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p297/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p297/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p297/r5.claim: The successful are content with God's will through prosperity and hardship, fulfilling others' rights when favoured and remaining patient when tried.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p297/r5.anchor: they showed patience and resolve and expressed contentment

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p315/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p315/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p315/r2.claim: Having succeeded in their trial and become worthy of Paradise, the contented souls are invited to join God's servants close to Him and enter Paradise.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p315/r2.anchor: since they have become worthy of Paradise after succeeding in their trial, they should now join His near ones in Paradise.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p271/r22.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p271/r22.speaker: الضحاك
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p271/r22.claim: Entering God's Garden may mean entering His mercy.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p271/r23.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p271/r23.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p271/r23.claim: The majority take it as the Garden of eternity, the home of the righteous.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p271/r23.anchor: الثاني : الجنة التي هي دار الخلود ومسكن الأبرار , وهو قول الجمهور .

STUDYQURAN:89:intro/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:89:intro/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:89:intro/r2.claim: The surah's opening oaths lead into accounts of tyrants, human vacillation under fortune, rebuke of stinginess, Judgment Day, and the peaceful believing soul.
STUDYQURAN:89:intro/r2.anchor: The sūrah begins with a series of oaths (vv. 1–4) followed by brief descriptions of the punishments

CORPUSCORANICUM:89:1-5:kommentar/r5.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:1-5:kommentar/r5.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:1-5:kommentar/r5.claim: Later additions in 23–24 and 27–30 bring the afterlife dimension into the sura and help decode the enigmatic oath.
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:1-5:kommentar/r5.anchor: Spätere Zusätze (V. 23.24 und V. 27–30) tragen diese eschatologische Dimension dann auch in die vorliegende Sure ein

CORPUSCORANICUM:89:21-26:kommentar/r5.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:21-26:kommentar/r5.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:21-26:kommentar/r5.claim: Verses 23–24 and 27–30 are later insertions that expand the original four-verse eschatological unit and enact the oath's duality as an antithesis.
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:21-26:kommentar/r5.anchor: V. 23.24 sind wie V. 27–30 spätere Einschübe (s. o.), die das eschatologische Vierergesätz

THALABI:v10p203#2/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p203#2/r1.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص
THALABI:v10p203#2/r1.claim: The believer rests in a spacious grave, lit by Quran or a sunlike light, like a bride asleep until a loved one wakes her; the unbeliever is sent a foul, coarse covering and told to depart to torment.
THALABI:v10p203#2/r1.anchor: ثم يؤمر فيوسع عليه قبره سبعون ذراعا عرضه وسبعون ذراعا طوله وينبت له فيه الريحان

THALABI:v10p203#2/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p203#2/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
THALABI:v10p203#2/r3.claim: At Ibn Abbas's burial, a bird entered his coffin and was not seen leaving; the verse was recited at the grave, though its reciter was unseen.
THALABI:v10p203#2/r3.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير قال: مات ابن عباس بالطائف فجاء طائر لم ير على خلقه

THALABI:v10p204/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p204/r4.speaker: مقاتل والقرظي وأبو عبيدة
THALABI:v10p204/r4.claim: They take 'enter among My servants' and 'enter My garden' as an inverted sequence meaning enter Paradise with God's servants.
THALABI:v10p204/r4.anchor: فادخلي في عبادي قال بعضهم: يعني مع عبادي جنتي في معنى الآية تقديم وتأخير

QASHANI:89:27-30/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:89:27-30/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:89:27-30/r4.claim: Entering God’s garden means the garden particular to Him, the garden of the essence.

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3429#5/r8.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3429#5/r8.speaker: الحسن
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3429#5/r8.claim: Al-Hasan says that when God takes a believer, the soul and God are mutually pleased; He then takes it into Paradise among His righteous servants.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3429#5/r8.anchor: عن الحسن رضي الله عنه في قوله : يا ايتها النفس المطمئنة الاية قال : ان الله اذا اراد قبض عبده المؤمن اطمانت النفس اليه

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3431/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3431/r1.speaker: أبو صالح
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3431/r1.claim: Abu Salih says return to God is the soul's departure from the world at death; on Resurrection it is told to enter among God's servants and into Paradise.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3431/r1.anchor: عن أبي صالح رضي الله عنه في قوله : ارجعي إلى ربك قال : هذا عند الموت رجوعها إلى ربها خروجها من الدنيا

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3431/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3431/r2.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3431/r2.claim: Qatada says the tranquil soul is a believer reassured by God's promise and that entering among His servants means joining the righteous.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3431/r2.anchor: عن قتادة يا ايتها النفس المطمئنة قال : هذا المؤمن اطمان إلى ما وعد الله

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3431/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3431/r4.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3431/r4.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam says the soul receives the good news of Paradise at death, resurrection, and the gathering.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3431/r4.anchor: عن زيد بن اسلم رضي الله عنه يا ايتها النفس المطمئنة الاية قال : بشرت بالجنة عند الموت وعند البعث ويوم الجمع

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3431/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3431/r5.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3431/r5.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr recounts that after Ibn Abbas died at Taif, an unseen bird entered his bier and did not emerge; the tranquil-soul verses were heard recited at his grave.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3431/r5.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير قال : مات ابن عباس بالطائف ، فجاء طير لم ير على خلقه ، فدخل نعشه ثم لم ير خارجا منه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p340/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p340/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p340/r3.claim: The passage ends the warnings with glad tidings for believers guided by the Quran, following the Quran's pattern of joining promise to warning to encourage good and deter evil.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p340/r3.anchor: ختم الكلام بالبشارة للمؤمنين الذين تذكروا بالقرآن واتبعوا هديه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p341/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p341/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p341/r3.claim: The first-person suffixes in My servants and My Paradise shift from the preceding third-person address.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p341/r3.anchor: والإضمار في قوله : { في عبادي } وقوله : { جنتي } التفات من الغيبة إلى التكلم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p343/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p343/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p343/r4.claim: Entering among God's servants and His Paradise details the general glad tiding, repeating the joy of the promised soul.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p343/r4.anchor: فهو تفصيل بعد الإجمال لتكرير إدخال السرور على أهلها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p343/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p343/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p343/r7.claim: Calling it My Paradise is an honorific attribution, as in the description of a seat of truth with a powerful king.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p343/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p343/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p343/r8.claim: The first-person attribution to Paradise makes the shift from God's mention in the third person aesthetically apt.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p343/r8.anchor: وهذه الإضافة هي مما يزيد الالتفات إلى ضمير التكلم حسنا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p343/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p343/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p343/r9.claim: Repeating the command to enter, rather than using one command with both objects, emphasizes Paradise itself and secures the hearers' joy.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p343/r9.anchor: فلم يقل : فادخلي جنتي في عبادي للاهتمام بالدخول

TUSTARI:89:30/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:89:30/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:89:30/r1.claim: There are two paradises: the Garden itself, and life through divine life and permanence through divine permanence.
TUSTARI:89:30/r1.anchor: قال سهل: الجنة جنتان: أحدهما الجنة نفسها، والأخرى حياة بحياة وبقاء ببقاء.

TUSTARI:89:30/r2.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:89:30/r2.speaker: author
TUSTARI:89:30/r2.claim: A report says the angels direct the solitary to their homes in Paradise, but they answer that they withdrew only for God and seek a good life with no other object.
TUSTARI:89:30/r2.anchor: كما روي في الخبر: يقول الملائكة للمنفردين يوم القيامة: امضوا إلى منازلكم في الجنة،

FARRA:v3p262/r5.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p262/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
FARRA:v3p262/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās alone reads “enter among My servant” and “enter My Garden” in the singular; the common reading has “My servants.”
FARRA:v3p262/r5.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس وحده: «فادخلي في عبدي ، وادخلي جنتي» والعوام (في عبادي)

KASHSHAF:89:30/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:89:30/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:89:30/r1.claim: Enter my Garden may mean enter it with God's servants.

KASHSHAF:89:30/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:89:30/r2.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF:89:30/r2.claim: Alternatively, nafs means the spirit, which is told to enter the bodies of God's servants.
KASHSHAF:89:30/r2.anchor: وقيل : النفس الروح .   ومعناه : فادخلي في أجساد عبادي

KASHSHAF:89:30/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:89:30/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
KASHSHAF:89:30/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas reads, Enter into My servant.

KASHSHAF:89:30/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:89:30/r4.speaker: ابن مسعود
KASHSHAF:89:30/r4.claim: Ibn Masʿud reads, Enter into My servant's body.

KASHSHAF:89:30/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:89:30/r5.speaker: أبي
KASHSHAF:89:30/r5.claim: Ubayy's reading says to come to one's Lord, content and pleasing, then enter His servant.
KASHSHAF:89:30/r5.anchor: وقرأ أبيّ : «ائتي ربك راضية مرضية ،   ادخلي في عبدي »

KASHSHAF:89:30/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:89:30/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:89:30/r6.claim: Some say the verse was revealed about Hamza; another says Khubayb, whose face God turned toward the qibla despite attempts to turn it away; the apparent sense is general.
KASHSHAF:89:30/r6.anchor: وقيل : نزلت في حمزة بن عبد المطلب .   وقيل : في خبيب بن عدي

KASHSHAF:89:30/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:89:30/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
KASHSHAF:89:30/r7.claim: A report promises forgiveness for reciting Surat al-Fajr during the ten nights and light on Resurrection Day when reciting it on other days.
KASHSHAF:89:30/r7.anchor: من قرأ سورة الفجر في الليالي العشر غفر له

MUQATIL:89:27-30/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:89:27-30/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:89:27-30/r3.claim: Entering among God's servants means entering His mercy, and entering the Garden is entering it through that mercy.
MUQATIL:89:27-30/r3.anchor: يعني في رحمتى { وادخلي } من رحمتي في { جنتي }

NASAFI-FULL:v4p339#4/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p339#4/r1.speaker: أبو عبيدة
NASAFI-FULL:v4p339#4/r1.claim: Abu Ubayda explains “enter among My servants” as entering with them or among God's chosen servants.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p339#4/r1.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة أى مع عبادى أوبين عبادى أى خواصى

NASAFI-FULL:v4p339#4/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p339#4/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p339#4/r2.claim: Another interpretation takes the soul as the spirit, entering the bodies of God's servants, supported by Ibn Masud's reading “into My servant's body.”
NASAFI-FULL:v4p339#4/r2.anchor: وقيل النفس الروح ومعناه فادخلى فى أجسام عبادى كقراءة عبد الله بن مسعود فى جسد عبدى

NASAFI-FULL:v4p339#4/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p339#4/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p339#4/r3.claim: A story says a strange bird entered Ibn Abbas's bier at his death in Taif and this verse was recited at his grave, though the reciter was unknown.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p339#4/r3.anchor: ولما مات بن عباس بالطائف جاء طائر لم ير على خلقته فدخل فى نعشه

NASAFI-FULL:v4p339#4/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p339#4/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p339#4/r4.claim: The verse is said to concern Hamza or Khubayb ibn Adi; in a report, God turned Khubayb's face toward the qibla after his prayer and no one could turn it back.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p339#4/r4.anchor: قيل نزلت فى حمزة بن عبد المطلب وقيل فى خبيب بن عدى الذى صلبه أهل مكة

NASAFI-FULL:v4p339#4/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p339#4/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p339#4/r5.claim: The verse applies generally to believers because the lesson follows the general wording rather than a particular occasion.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p339#4/r5.anchor: وقيل هى عامة فى المؤمنين إذ العبرة لعموم اللفظ لا لخصوص السبب

QURTUBI-FULL:89:27-30/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:89:27-30/r11.speaker: الجمهور
QURTUBI-FULL:89:27-30/r11.claim: The majority understand Paradise as the everlasting home and dwelling of the righteous.
QURTUBI-FULL:89:27-30/r11.anchor: والجمهور على أن الجنة هي دار الخلود التي هي مسكن الأبرار، ودار الصالحين والأخيار

QURTUBI-FULL:89:27-30/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:89:27-30/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:89:27-30/r14.claim: The soul is to enter God’s Paradise together with the righteous servants.

QUTB-ZILAL:89:30/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:89:30/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:89:30/r1.claim: Entering God's garden means entering His protection and mercy.

QUTB-ZILAL:89:30/r2.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:89:30/r2.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:89:30/r2.claim: The whole address gives a foretaste of Paradise's secure, gentle closeness, centered on the soul's trust in God and His decree in ease and hardship.
QUTB-ZILAL:89:30/r2.anchor: والمطمئنة فلا ترتاع في يوم الهول الرعيب

RAZI-FULL:v31p162/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p162/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p162/r7.claim: Entering God's Garden refers to bodily happiness, complementary to the spiritual happiness of joining the servants.
RAZI-FULL:v31p162/r7.anchor: ثم قال : { وادخلى جنتى } وهذا إشارة إلى السعادة الجسمانية

RAZI-FULL:v31p162/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p162/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p162/r9.claim: Bodily Paradise comes only after the great Resurrection, so its entrance is joined with wa rather than fa.
RAZI-FULL:v31p162/r9.anchor: ولما كانت الجنة الجسمانية لا يحصل الفوز بها إلا بعد قيام القيامة الكبرى ، لا جرم قال : { وادخلى جنتى

STUDYQURAN:89:27/r17.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:89:27/r17.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:89:27/r17.claim: The Hereafter contains progressive levels, from lower to higher gardens; most take God's Garden as Paradise generally, while some identify it with the highest Garden of the Divine Essence in God's Presence.
STUDYQURAN:89:27/r17.anchor: the Hereafter has progressive levels with lower and higher gardens

TAB:89:27/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:89:27/r9.speaker: أبو أسامة بن زيد عن أبيه
TAB:89:27/r9.claim: A report says the tranquil soul is promised the Garden at death, on the Day of Gathering, and at resurrection.
TAB:89:27/r9.anchor: عن أُسامة بن زيد ،   عن أبيه ،   في قوله :  يا أيّتُها النّفْسُ المُطْمَئِنّةُ قال :  بُشّرت بالجنة

TAB:89:29/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:89:29/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB:89:29/r1.claim: One view says the angels call the believer's soul at resurrection to return to its body; Ibn ʿAbbās says tranquil souls return to bodies on that day.
TAB:89:29/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس ،   قوله :  يا أيّتُها النّفْسُ المُطْمَئِنّةُ ارْجِعي إلى رَبّكِ رَاضِيَةً مَرْضِيّةً قال :  تردّ الأرواح

TAB:89:29/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:89:29/r2.speaker: الضحاك
TAB:89:29/r2.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says God orders souls to return to bodies at resurrection, when they come to Him as He first created them.
TAB:89:29/r2.anchor: سمعت الضحاك يقول في قوله :  فادْخُلِي فِي عبادِي وَادْخُلِي جَنّتِي يأمر الله الأرواح يوم القيامة أن ترجع إلى الأجساد

TAB:89:29/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:89:29/r5.speaker: author
TAB:89:29/r5.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers the resurrection interpretation because the following words tell the soul to enter among God's servants and into His Garden.
TAB:89:29/r5.anchor: وأولى القولين في ذلك بالصواب القول الذي ذكرناه عن ابن عباس والضحاك ،   أن ذلك إنما يقال لهم

TAB:89:29/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:89:29/r6.speaker: قتادة
TAB:89:29/r6.claim: Qatāda interprets entry among God's servants as joining the righteous servants.
TAB:89:29/r6.anchor: عن قتادة ،   قوله :  فادْخُلِي فِي عِبادِي قال :  ادخلي في عبادي الصالحين وَادْخُلِي جَنّتِي .

TAB:89:29/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:89:29/r7.speaker: محمد بن مزاحم
TAB:89:29/r7.claim: Muḥammad ibn Muzāḥim says entering among God's servants means entering His obedience, and entering His Garden means entering His mercy.
TAB:89:29/r7.anchor: عن محمد بن مزاحم أخي الضحاك بن مُزاحم :  فادْخُلِي فِي عِبادِي قال :  في طاعتي وَادْخُلِي جَنّتِي قال :  في رحمتي .

TAB:89:29/r10.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:89:29/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB:89:29/r10.claim: A variant attributed to Ibn ʿAbbās reads the singular servant instead of plural servants; al-Kalbī says this refers to the spirit returning to its body.
TAB:89:29/r10.anchor: عن ابن عباس ،   أنه قرأها :  «فادْخُلِي فِي عَبْدِي » على التوحيد .

TAB:89:30/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:89:30/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB:89:30/r1.claim: One view says the angels call the believer's soul at resurrection to return to its body; Ibn ʿAbbās says tranquil souls return to bodies on that day.
TAB:89:30/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس ،   قوله :  يا أيّتُها النّفْسُ المُطْمَئِنّةُ ارْجِعي إلى رَبّكِ رَاضِيَةً مَرْضِيّةً قال :  تردّ الأرواح

TAB:89:30/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:89:30/r2.speaker: الضحاك
TAB:89:30/r2.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says God orders souls to return to bodies at resurrection, when they come to Him as He first created them.
TAB:89:30/r2.anchor: سمعت الضحاك يقول في قوله :  فادْخُلِي فِي عبادِي وَادْخُلِي جَنّتِي يأمر الله الأرواح يوم القيامة أن ترجع إلى الأجساد

TAB:89:30/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:89:30/r5.speaker: author
TAB:89:30/r5.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers the resurrection interpretation because the following words tell the soul to enter among God's servants and into His Garden.
TAB:89:30/r5.anchor: وأولى القولين في ذلك بالصواب القول الذي ذكرناه عن ابن عباس والضحاك ،   أن ذلك إنما يقال لهم

TAB:89:30/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:89:30/r6.speaker: قتادة
TAB:89:30/r6.claim: Qatāda interprets entry among God's servants as joining the righteous servants.
TAB:89:30/r6.anchor: عن قتادة ،   قوله :  فادْخُلِي فِي عِبادِي قال :  ادخلي في عبادي الصالحين وَادْخُلِي جَنّتِي .

TAB:89:30/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:89:30/r7.speaker: محمد بن مزاحم
TAB:89:30/r7.claim: Muḥammad ibn Muzāḥim says entering among God's servants means entering His obedience, and entering His Garden means entering His mercy.
TAB:89:30/r7.anchor: عن محمد بن مزاحم أخي الضحاك بن مُزاحم :  فادْخُلِي فِي عِبادِي قال :  في طاعتي وَادْخُلِي جَنّتِي قال :  في رحمتي .

TAB:89:30/r10.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:89:30/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB:89:30/r10.claim: A variant attributed to Ibn ʿAbbās reads the singular servant instead of plural servants; al-Kalbī says this refers to the spirit returning to its body.
TAB:89:30/r10.anchor: عن ابن عباس ،   أنه قرأها :  «فادْخُلِي فِي عَبْدِي » على التوحيد .

TAB-FULL:v24p397/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p397/r2.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v24p397/r2.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says God commands the spirits at Resurrection to return to their bodies and come to Him as first created.
TAB-FULL:v24p397/r2.anchor: سمعت الضحاك، يقول في قوله: {فادخلي في عبادي وادخلي جنتي} [الفجر: 30] : يأمر الله الأرواح يوم القيامة أن ترجع إلى الأجساد

TAB-FULL:v24p397/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p397/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p397/r5.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers the Resurrection interpretation reported from Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Ḍaḥḥāk because the next phrase speaks of entering among God's servants and His Garden.
TAB-FULL:v24p397/r5.anchor: وأولى القولين في ذلك بالصواب القول الذي ذكرناه عن ابن عباس والضحاك، أن ذلك إنما يقال لهم عند رد الأرواح في الأجساد يوم البعث

TAB-FULL:v24p397/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p397/r6.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v24p397/r6.claim: Qatāda explains entry among God's servants as joining the righteous servants.
TAB-FULL:v24p397/r6.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {فادخلي في عبادي} [الفجر: 29] قال: ادخلي في عبادي الصالحين

TAB-FULL:v24p397/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p397/r7.speaker: محمد بن مزاحم
TAB-FULL:v24p397/r7.claim: Muḥammad b. Muzāḥim interprets entry among God's servants as entry into God's obedience and His Garden as His mercy.
TAB-FULL:v24p397/r7.anchor: عن محمد بن مزاحم، أخي الضحاك بن مزاحم: {فادخلي في عبادي} [الفجر: 29] قال: في طاعتي {وادخلي جنتي} [الفجر: 30] قال: في رحمتي

TABATABAI:89:29-30/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:89:29-30/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:89:29-30/r1.claim: The tranquil soul is admitted among God’s servants because it has abandoned independence, accepted God’s truth, and submits its being, acts, and choices to Him; entry among the servants affirms complete servitude.
TABATABAI:89:29-30/r1.anchor: لما اطمأن إلى ربه انقطع عن دعوى الاستقلال ورضي بما هو الحق من ربه

TABATABAI:89:29-30/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:89:29-30/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:89:29-30/r2.claim: Entering God’s garden identifies the soul’s abode; the possessive “My garden” is a special honor and occurs nowhere else in the Qurʾān.
TABATABAI:89:29-30/r2.anchor: وفي إضافة الجنة إلى ضمير التكلم تشريف خاص، ولا يوجد في كلامه تعالى إضافة الجنة إلى نفسه

ZAJJAJ:v5p324/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p324/r7.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p324/r7.claim: The majority reading and interpretation are fī ʿibādī followed by wadkhulī jannatī.
ZAJJAJ:v5p324/r7.anchor: والأكثر في القراءة والتفسير: (فادخلي في عبادي (29) وادخلي جنتي (30).

TABRISI:89:29-30/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:89:29-30/r15.speaker: author
TABRISI:89:29-30/r15.claim: “My Garden” is the Paradise promised to the servants and prepared with its delights.
TABRISI:89:29-30/r15.anchor: التي وعدتكم بها وأعددت نعيمكم فيها

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:89:27-30/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:89:27-30/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:89:27-30/r5.claim: She is invited to enter God's Paradise.

ELMALILI:89:27-30/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:89:27-30/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:89:27-30/r4.claim: Another interpretation has the soul join the ranks of the near ones and shine through their light as pure spirits reflect one another.
ELMALILI:89:27-30/r4.anchor: Mukarrebîn sırasına dizil ve onların nûrlarıyla parla

ELMALILI:89:27-30/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:89:27-30/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:89:27-30/r5.claim: Another interpretation understands the entry as the soul entering bodies and then entering the abode of reward with them.
ELMALILI:89:27-30/r5.anchor: Cesetlere gir, onlarla birlikte dâr-ı sevâba gir

ELMALILI:89:27-30#2/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:89:27-30#2/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:89:27-30#2/r16.claim: Exegetes differ on whether this address comes at death, resurrection, or after the reckoning; the author considers the last timing most apparent from the context.
ELMALILI:89:27-30#2/r16.anchor: Bunda üç kavil vardır: Ölüm zamanında olması, ba‘s zamanında

ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r3.claim: On that reading, entering God’s garden means entering the abode of reward together with the servants.
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r3.anchor: birlikte dâr-ı sevab olan cennete duhûldür

ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r9.speaker: Ebû Sâlih
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r9.claim: Abu Salih says returning to the Lord is at death as departure from the world, while entering among the servants and entering Paradise are commands at resurrection.
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r9.anchor: Bu âyette ٱرْجِعِىٓ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكِ inde’l-mevttir

ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r10.claim: Though Abu Salih’s reading seems apparent, the context favors the address after resurrection and completed reckoning; the reports can fit by treating each death as a person’s resurrection or the commands together as a unit.
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r10.anchor: bu hitâbın da o güne ait olması iktizâ edeceğinden ba‘de’l-ba‘s

ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r11.speaker: Zeyd b. Eslem
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r11.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam reports that the tranquil soul is given this address at death, resurrection, and the gathering, and is promised Paradise.
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r11.anchor: mutmainne ölüm sırasında ve ba‘s sırasında ve cem‘günü cennet ile tebşir olunmuştur

ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r12.claim: The majority understand an omitted “God will say” from the preceding context, making the address and commands declarative and creative rather than legislative.
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r12.anchor: cumhûrun muhtârı budur. Buna göre bu hitâbın ve emirlerin teşrî‘î değil tekvînî olması

ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r13.claim: The author also considers a direct, legislative divine address at the surah’s conclusion plausible; separation from what precedes highlights that the tranquil souls themselves should hear it.
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r13.anchor: bunun nüfûs-i mutmainne tarafından re’sen ve bilhassa istimâ‘ı maksud olduğuna tenbih için

ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r18.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r18.speaker: author
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r18.claim: Entering God’s garden means entering Paradise with those servants in the hereafter, signaling the tranquil soul’s good final outcome.
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r18.anchor: âhirette onlarla beraber cennete dâhil olmak ile emir olmuş

ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r19.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r19.speaker: author
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r19.claim: The life of a tranquil soul among the righteous is like the ten nights before Eid al-Adha, and its entry into Paradise is the dawn of the greatest festival of bliss.
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r19.anchor: dünya ömrü îd-i adhâya tekaddüm eden bir leyâl-i aşr

ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r20.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r20.speaker: author
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r20.claim: The commentator prays that he and his readers return to God content and accepted, join His sincere servants, and reach Paradise and the vision of God.
ELMALILI:89:27-30#3/r20.anchor: bu abd-i hakīri ve bunları hüsn-i nazarla okuyup ona hayırhah olanları

CORPUSCORANICUM:89:29-30:anmerkung/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:29-30:anmerkung/r1.speaker: Neuwirth
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:29-30:anmerkung/r1.claim: Neuwirth rejects the Kufan division between the verses because the two related imperatives should not be separated.

CORPUSCORANICUM:89:29-30:anmerkung/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:29-30:anmerkung/r2.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:29-30:anmerkung/r2.claim: The author counters that ʿibādī and jannatī form an approximate rhyme if nonclassical vowel and consonant variations are allowed, as in other Quranic pairs.
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:29-30:anmerkung/r2.anchor: Dagegen steht allerdings der zumindest näherungsweise Reimcharakter von ʿibādi / ǧannati

CORPUSCORANICUM:89:29-30:anmerkung/r3.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:29-30:anmerkung/r3.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:29-30:anmerkung/r3.claim: For ʿabd, the note refers to 53:10.
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:29-30:anmerkung/r3.anchor: Zum Ausdruck ʿabd vgl. die Anmerkung zu 53:10.

CORPUSCORANICUM:89:27-30:kommentar/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:27-30:kommentar/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:27-30:kommentar/r1.claim: Later verses 27–30 add a positive afterlife ending to the earlier threat-only conclusion, pairing entry into the Garden with the Hell mentioned in verse 23.

CORPUSCORANICUM:89:27-30:kommentar/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:27-30:kommentar/r2.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:27-30:kommentar/r2.claim: All three insertions use direct speech: the human responds to worldly allotment and threatened Hell, then God's address to the trusting soul and servants supersedes those negative statements.
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:27-30:kommentar/r2.anchor: Auffällig ist, dass alle drei Einschübe – V. 15.16, V. 23.24 und V. 27–30 – wörtliche Reden enthalten

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:89:27/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:89:27/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:89:27/r3.claim: Addressing the person directly without an introductory afterlife formula is a graceful, warm honor that lets the promise of otherworldly happiness reach into this life.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:89:27/r3.anchor: doğrudan insana hitap edilmesi, Cenâb-ı Hakk’ın bu yapıdaki kullarına çok güzel bir iltifatı

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:89:27/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:89:27/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:89:27/r6.claim: God's calling the admitted to Paradise “My servants” is a supreme honor; their final gift is divine pleasure, greater than all other blessings.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:89:27/r6.anchor: “Benim kullarım” diye anması iltifatların en güzelidir

ALUSI-FULL:v30p131#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p131#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p131#2/r1.claim: The command to enter the garden is coordinated with the preceding one: joining God's servants is spiritual happiness, while the garden is bodily happiness; the first is placed first as superior.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p131#2/r1.anchor: وكان الأمر بالدخول في جملة عباد الله تعالى الصالحين إشارة إلى السعادة الروحانية

ALUSI-FULL:v30p131#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p131#2/r2.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v30p131#2/r2.claim: Abu Hayyan explains the preposition with entering a nonliteral sphere and its omission with a genuine container such as the garden.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p131#2/r2.anchor: قال أبو حيان لأن المدخول فيه إن كان غير ظرف حقيقي تعدى إليه في الأستعمال بفي

ALUSI-FULL:v30p131#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p131#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p131#2/r3.claim: One view reads “return to your Lord” as returning to the promised destination, meaning Paradise and the company of the righteous if the address comes after judgment.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p131#2/r3.anchor: وقيل المراد ارجعي إلى موعد ربك واستظهر أن المراد بموعده تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v30p131#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p131#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p131#2/r4.claim: To answer the objection that returning implies prior residence in Paradise, one says souls were potentially present in Adam while he was in the garden; a similar interpretation of 28:85 takes “return” as Paradise, but it depends on identifying Adam's garden with the final one.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p131#2/r4.anchor: وأجيب بتحقق هذا المقتضى بناء على وجودها بالقوة في ظهر آدم عليه السلام

ALUSI-FULL:v30p131#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p131#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p131#2/r5.claim: Another construes “return to your Lord” as returning to His command, meaning a gracious treatment, an honored station, or a comparable state.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p131#2/r5.anchor: وقيل المراد ارجعي إلى أمر ربك واستظهر أن المراد بالأمر على ذلك التقدير

ALUSI-FULL:v30p131#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p131#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p131#2/r6.claim: A further view makes it a return to God's honor, understood generally, because the soul was in the intermediate realm or after resurrection or judgment.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p131#2/r6.anchor: وقيل المراد ارجعي إلى كرامة ربك ويراد جنس كرامته سبحانه والرجوع إليه باعتبار

ALUSI-FULL:v30p131#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p131#2/r7.speaker: عكرمة والضحاك
ALUSI-FULL:v30p131#2/r7.claim: Ikrima and al-Dahhak place the address at resurrection and understand the soul as the person, with God as Lord; some supply an omitted noun for the return to His station.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p131#2/r7.anchor: وعن عكرمة والضحاك أن ذلك القول عند البعث فقيل النفس بمعنى الذات أيضا

ALUSI-FULL:v30p131#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p131#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p131#2/r8.claim: Another reading makes “soul” the spirit and “Lord” its owner, the body: it returns to its earthly body and then enters among God's servants and His reward.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p131#2/r8.anchor: وقيل للنفس بمعنى الروح والمراد بالرب الصاحب وفسر بالجسد وباقي الآية على حالة

ALUSI-FULL:v30p131#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p131#2/r9.speaker: ابن عباس وابن جبير
ALUSI-FULL:v30p131#2/r9.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas and Ibn Jubayr reads “among My servants” as “among the bodies of My servants,” with the plural understood generically.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p131#2/r9.anchor: وجاء هذا في رواية عن ابن عباس وابن جبير ولا يضر الإفراد أولا والجمع ثانيا

ALUSI-FULL:v30p131#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p131#2/r10.speaker: ابن زيد
ALUSI-FULL:v30p131#2/r10.claim: Ibn Zayd and a group say the address comes at death, supported by a report transmitted from Saʿid ibn Jubayr.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p131#2/r10.anchor: وقال ابن زيد وجماعة أن ذلك القول عند الموت وأيد بما أخرجه عبد بن حميد

ALUSI-FULL:v30p132/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p132/r1.speaker: النبي
ALUSI-FULL:v30p132/r1.claim: A report says the verse was recited before the Prophet; Abu Bakr praised it, and the Prophet said an angel would address him with it at death. Al-Alusi also cites a similar version in al-Hakim al-Tirmidhi.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p132/r1.anchor: قال قرئت عند النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم يا أيتها النفس المطمئنة الآية فقال أبو بكر

ALUSI-FULL:v30p132/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p132/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p132/r2.claim: On the death-time interpretation, “soul” means spirit: it returns at death to God's holy realm, enters the company of the near servants and the garden prepared for tranquil souls.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p132/r2.anchor: والنفس عليه بمعنى الروح والمعنى على ما قيل ارجعي بالموت إلى عالم قدس ربك

ALUSI-FULL:v30p132/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p132/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p132/r3.claim: On this view the first entry follows death without delay, while entry into the garden of lasting residence follows at resurrection; because it is certain, both commands can nevertheless use immediate sequencing.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p132/r3.anchor: وهذان الدخولان يعقبان الرجوع إلا أن الدخول الأول يعقبه بلا تراخ قبل يوم القيامة

ALUSI-FULL:v30p132/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p132/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p132/r4.claim: Other timings allow both entries immediately if the soul joins a righteous company and enjoys Paradise temporarily before resurrection; reports describe believers' spirits in birds in Paradise and a share of Paradise after death.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p132/r4.anchor: ففي الحديث أن أرواح المؤمنين في حواصل طيور في الجنة وفي بعض الآثار إذا مات المؤمن أعطى نصف الجنة

ALUSI-FULL:v30p132/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p132/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p132/r5.claim: The image of souls like polished mirrors reflecting one another's lights and increasing knowledge is dismissed by al-Alusi as rhetorical speculation.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p132/r5.anchor: وذكر في وجه إدخالها مع الأرواح القدسية كالمرايا المصقولة فإذا انضم بعضها إلى بعض

ALUSI-FULL:v30p132#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p132#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p132#2/r1.claim: Abu Salih says “return to your Lord” refers to death and leaving the world, while entry among God's servants and into His garden occurs at resurrection.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p132#2/r1.anchor: قال في الآية ارجعي إلى ربك هذا عنوا الموت

ALUSI-FULL:v30p132#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p132#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p132#2/r2.claim: Another interpretation places the address after death but before resurrection and takes “return” as return to the body for questioning by the two angels.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p132#2/r2.anchor: وقيل أن هذا القول بعد الموت وقبل القيامة والمراد برجوعها إلى ربها رجوعها إلى جسدها

ALUSI-FULL:v30p132#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p132#2/r3.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي
ALUSI-FULL:v30p132#2/r3.claim: Muhammad ibn Kaʿb says the believer is shown his future home in Paradise at death, then told to return to the body, pleased with the reward shown, until Munkar and Nakir question him.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p132#2/r3.anchor: أخرج ابن المنذر عن محمد بن كعب القرظي أنه قال في الآية أن المؤمن إذا مات أرى منزله

ALUSI-FULL:v30p132#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p132#2/r4.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
ALUSI-FULL:v30p132#2/r4.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam says the believer is given the good news of Paradise at death, at resurrection, and on the day of gathering.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p132#2/r4.anchor: وقيل أنه في مواطن ثلاثة أخرج ابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم عن زيد بن أسلم

ALUSI-FULL:v30p132#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p132#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p132#2/r5.claim: A reading that applies these commands to every time in worldly life makes them calls to continual obedience and good works, but al-Alusi says it should not count as a valid interpretation.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p132#2/r5.anchor: وقيل يجوز أن يكون ذلك في سائر أوقات النفس في حياتها الدنيا

ALUSI-FULL:v30p132#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p132#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p132#2/r6.claim: Al-Alusi says the address appears general across the proposed occasions rather than restricted to a single one.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p132#2/r6.anchor: وأيا ما كان من الأوجه فالظاهر العموم فيها

ALUSI-FULL:v30p132#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p132#2/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v30p132#2/r7.claim: One report says the verse was revealed about ʿUthman ibn ʿAffan after he bought the well of Rumah and made it a public watering place; other proposed occasions name Hamza or Khubayb.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p132#2/r7.anchor: وإن أخرج ابن أبي حاتم من طريق جويبر عن الضحاك عن ابن عباس أنها نزلت في عثمان

ALUSI-FULL:v30p132#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p132#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p132#2/r8.claim: The named Companions, including ʿUthman, Hamza, and Khubayb, are examples rather than exclusive referents; the occasion's form necessarily falls within the verse.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p132#2/r8.anchor: فتفسير النفس المذكورة بأحد هؤلاء المذكورين كما نقل عن بعض من باب التمثيل

ALUSI-FULL:v30p132#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p132#2/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v30p132#2/r9.claim: A report through Ibn Mardawayh identifies the tranquil soul as the Prophet; al-Alusi likewise treats this as an illustrative application.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p132#2/r9.anchor: وينبغي أن يتحمل قول ابن عباس في تلك النفس كما أخرجه عنه ابن مردويه هو النبي

ALUSI-FULL:v30p132#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p132#2/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p132#2/r10.claim: Some readings suggest that souls existed before bodies in the realm of the unseen; this issue is famous, while most theologians and Plato's school say souls are created when bodies are ready.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p132#2/r10.anchor: وأشعرت الآية على بعض أوجهها بأن الأرواح مخلوقة قبل الأبدان ومقرها إذ ذاك في عالم الملكوت

ALUSI-FULL:v30p132#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p132#2/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v30p132#2/r11.claim: Ibn Abbas, ʿIkrima, al-Dahhak, Mujahid, Abu Jaʿfar, Abu Salih, and the Yamani read “among My servant” in the singular, understood generically.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p132#2/r11.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس وعكرمة والضحاك ومجاهد وأبو جعفر وأبو صالح وأبو شيخ اليماني في عبدي

ALUSI-FULL:v30p132#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p132#2/r12.speaker: السادة الصوفية
ALUSI-FULL:v30p132#2/r12.claim: Sufi teachers describe three ranks of the soul in this verse: tranquil, pleased, and approved; al-Alusi leaves their detailed exposition to their books.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p132#2/r12.anchor: وللسادة الصوفية قدست نفوسهم كلام طويل في تقسيم مراتب النفس وقالوا أن الآية متضمنة لمراتب ثلاث

ALUSI-FULL:v30p132#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p132#2/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p132#2/r13.claim: Al-Alusi quotes a supplication taught by the Prophet asking God for a tranquil soul that believes in meeting Him, accepts His decree, and is content with His gift.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p132#2/r13.anchor: وأنا أقول كما علم رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم بعض الصحابة على ما أخرج الطبراني

ALUSI-FULL:v30p133/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p133/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p133/r1.claim: The next surah is Meccan according to most, though complete Medinan and mixed datings are also proposed; the reference to this city weighs against the latter, and al-Zamakhshari claims consensus on its Meccan origin.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p133/r1.anchor: مكية في قول الجمهور بتمامها وقيل مدنية بتمامها وقيل مدنية إلا أربع آيات من أولها

ALUSI-FULL:v30p133/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p133/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p133/r2.claim: Some reports suggest the opening of the next surah was revealed in Mecca after the conquest.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p133/r2.anchor: وسيأتي إن شاء الله تعالى أن في بعض الخبار ما هو ظاهر في نزول صدرها بمكة بعد الفتح

ALUSI-FULL:v30p133/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p133/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p133/r3.claim: The transition links the surahs: after condemnation of hoarding wealth and neglecting the needy, the next passage names freeing slaves and feeding in famine; the tranquil soul is likewise linked to the path to contentment.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p133/r3.anchor: ولما ذم سبحانه فيما قبلها من أحب المال وأكل التراث أكلا لما ولم يحض على طعام المسكين ذكر جل وعلا فيها الخصال

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p423#2/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p423#2/r8.speaker: أبو صالح
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p423#2/r8.claim: Abu Salih says ‘return to your Lord’ is spoken when the soul leaves worldly life, while ‘enter among my servants and enter my Paradise’ is spoken at resurrection.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p423#2/r8.anchor: وقال أبو صالح في قوله: "ارجعي إلى ربك راضية مرضية" قال: هذا عند خروجها من الدنيا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p425/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p425/r1.speaker: أهل الإشارة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p425/r1.claim: Some mystically interpret the tranquil soul as attached to worldly life, told to return to God by abandoning it and following the path of the afterlife.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p425/r1.anchor: وقال بعض أهل الإشارة: يا أيتها النفس المطمئنة إلى الدنيا ارجعي إلى الله بتركها

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p425/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p425/r2.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p425/r2.claim: Saʿid b. Jubayr recounts Ibn Abbas’s funeral: a strange bird entered the bier and never emerged, and the full ‘tranquil soul’ verses were recited at the grave by an unknown voice.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p425/r2.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير: مات ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما بالطائف فشهدت جنازته، فجاء طائر لم [نر] (1)

BAYDAWI-FULL:89:28-30/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:89:28-30/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:89:28-30/r4.claim: Entering God's Garden is entry into the reward prepared for the soul.
BAYDAWI-FULL:89:28-30/r4.anchor: وادخلي دار ثوابي التي أعدت لك

BAYDAWI-FULL:89:28-30/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:89:28-30/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAYDAWI-FULL:89:28-30/r5.claim: A report promises forgiveness for reciting al-Fajr during the ten nights and a light on the Resurrection Day for reciting it at other times.
BAYDAWI-FULL:89:28-30/r5.anchor: من قرأ سورة الفجر في الليالي العشر غفر له

BIQAI-FULL:v8p423/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p423/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p423/r10.claim: God's garden is the Garden of Eden, the highest of the gardens.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p423/r10.anchor: أي وهي جنة عدن وهي أعلى الجنان

BIQAI-FULL:v8p423/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p423/r11.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
BIQAI-FULL:v8p423/r11.claim: Saʿīd b. Jubayr reports that a bird entered Ibn ʿAbbās's funeral bier and did not emerge; an unknown voice recited this verse at the grave.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p423/r11.anchor: سعيد بن بجير : مات ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما بالطائف

DURR-FULL:v8p513/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p513/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p513/r6.claim: A report from Ibn ʿAbbās says God invited people to buy the well of Rūma, which ʿUthmān bought and made available for public drinking; the verses were then revealed about him.
DURR-FULL:v8p513/r6.anchor: عن الضحاك عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: من يشتري بئر رومة نستعذب بها غفر الله له

DURR-FULL:v8p513#2/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p513#2/r11.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v8p513#2/r11.claim: Al-Ḥasan says when God takes a believer’s soul, it rests in God and both are pleased; it is admitted to Paradise among the righteous.
DURR-FULL:v8p513#2/r11.anchor: في قوله: {يا أيتها النفس المطمئنة} الآية قال: إن الله إذا أراد قبض عبده المؤمن

DURR-FULL:v8p515/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p515/r1.speaker: أبو صالح
DURR-FULL:v8p515/r1.claim: Abū Ṣāliḥ says return to God occurs at death as the soul leaves the world; at resurrection it is told to enter among God’s servants and into Paradise.
DURR-FULL:v8p515/r1.anchor: قوله: {ارجعي إلى ربك} قال: هذا عند الموت رجوعها إلى ربها خروجها من الدنيا

DURR-FULL:v8p515/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p515/r5.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p515/r5.claim: Qatāda identifies it as the believer who trusts God’s promise; entering among God’s servants means entering the righteous and Paradise.
DURR-FULL:v8p515/r5.anchor: عن قتادة {يا أيتها النفس المطمئنة} قال: هذا المؤمن اطمأن إلى ما وعد الله

DURR-FULL:v8p515/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p515/r9.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p515/r9.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam says the believer receives glad tidings of Paradise at death, resurrection, and the gathering.
DURR-FULL:v8p515/r9.anchor: عن زيد بن أسلم رضي الله عنه {يا أيتها النفس المطمئنة} الآية قال: بشرت بالجنة عند الموت وعند البعث ويوم الجمع

DURR-FULL:v8p515/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p515/r10.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
DURR-FULL:v8p515/r10.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr recounts a mysterious bird entering Ibn ʿAbbās’s coffin and never being seen again; the tranquil-soul verses were recited at his grave by an unknown person.
DURR-FULL:v8p515/r10.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير رضي الله عنه قال: مات ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما بالطائف فجاء طير لم تر عين خلقته فدخل نعشه

TAB:89:28/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:89:28/r7.speaker: محمد بن مزاحم
TAB:89:28/r7.claim: Muhammad ibn Muzahim takes God’s servants as His obedience and God’s garden as His mercy.
TAB:89:28/r7.anchor: عن محمد بن مزاحم أخي الضحاك بن مزاحم : فادخلي في عبادي قال : في طاعتي

TAB:89:28/r13.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:89:28/r13.speaker: الكلبي
TAB:89:28/r13.claim: Al-Kalbi’s singular reading means that the soul returns into the body.
TAB:89:28/r13.anchor: وفي قول الكلبيّ : «فادْخُلِي فِي عَبْدِي ، وَادْخُلِي فِي جَنّتِي »

BURHAN:v4p302/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p302/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p302/r1.claim: في has spatial containment senses: both place and contained thing may be physical or conceptual, or one physical and one abstract; the first is literal and the fourth metaphor is closest to literal.
BURHAN:v4p302/r1.anchor: للظرفية ثم تارة يكون الظرف والمظروف حسيين نحو زيد في الدار

ABUHAYYAN:89:30/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:89:30/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:89:30/r1.claim: The soul is to enter God’s Garden together with the servants just mentioned.

ABUHAYYAN:89:30/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:89:30/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:89:30/r6.claim: Entering a nonliteral domain takes fī, while a literal container usually follows the verb directly, explaining the different constructions.
ABUHAYYAN:89:30/r6.anchor: وتعدى فادخلي أولاً بفي ، وثانياً بغير فاء ، وذلك أنه إذا كان المدخول فيه غير ظرف حقيقي تعددت إليه بفي

ABUHAYYAN:89:30/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:89:30/r7.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN:89:30/r7.claim: Some say the verse refers to ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān, others to Ḥamza, and others to Khubayb ibn ʿAdī.
ABUHAYYAN:89:30/r7.anchor: قيل : في عثمان بن عفان . وقيل : في حمزة . وقيل : في خبيب بن عدي

ALUSI:89:29/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:29/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI:89:29/r2.claim: Entering God’s Garden is the bodily happiness promised to the tranquil soul, prepared for such souls.
ALUSI:89:29/r2.anchor: وادخلي جنتي التي أعددتها لذوي النفوس المطمئنة

ALUSI:89:29/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:29/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI:89:29/r3.claim: The first command signifies spiritual happiness through companionship with the righteous; the second signifies bodily happiness, and the superior spiritual reward is mentioned first, with the Garden completing it.
ALUSI:89:29/r3.anchor: إشارة إلى السعادة الروحانية لكمال استئناس النفس بالجليس الصالح والأمر بدخول الجنة إشارة إلى السعادة الجسمانية

ALUSI:89:29/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:29/r4.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI:89:29/r4.claim: Abu Hayyan explains that dukhūl takes fī with a figurative or nonliteral domain, but usually takes a real container directly.
ALUSI:89:29/r4.anchor: قال أبو حيان لأن المدخول فيه إن كان غير ظرف حقيقي تعدى إليه في الاستعمال بفي

ALUSI:89:29/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:29/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI:89:29/r5.claim: One reading takes ‘return to your Lord’s promise’ as the promised Garden and company of the righteous, spoken after the reckoning; the objection that this implies prior residence is answered by a potential existence in Adam’s loins while he was in the Garden.
ALUSI:89:29/r5.anchor: وقيل المراد ارجعي إلى موعد ربك واستظهر أن المراد بموعده تعالى

ALUSI:89:29/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:29/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI:89:29/r6.claim: The proposed prior existence is compared with reports from ʿAlī and Ibn ʿAbbās that maʿād in 28:85 means Paradise rather than Mecca; this works only if Adam’s Garden was the eschatological Garden, a strongly disputed identification discussed by Ibn al-Qayyim.
ALUSI:89:29/r6.anchor: على ما روى عن أمير المؤمنين علي كرم الله تعالى وجهه وعن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما من أن المراد بالمعاد الجنة دون مكة

ALUSI:89:29/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:29/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI:89:29/r7.claim: Another interpretation makes ‘return to your Lord’s command’ mean return to one of His affairs: His treatment of her without distress, placement in an honored station, or something similar.
ALUSI:89:29/r7.anchor: وقيل المراد ارجعي إلى أمر ربك واستظهر أن المراد بالأمر على ذلك التقدير

ALUSI:89:29/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:29/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI:89:29/r8.claim: A further view understands the return as return to God’s general favor, from the barzakh after death or from the period after resurrection but before judgment.
ALUSI:89:29/r8.anchor: وقيل المراد ارجعي إلى كرامة ربك ويراد جنس كرامته سبحانه

ALUSI:89:29/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:29/r9.speaker: عكرمة والضحاك
ALUSI:89:29/r9.claim: ʿIkrima and al-Ḍaḥḥāk place the address at resurrection; on one analysis nafs means the person, Lord means God, and an implied noun supplies the station to which she returns.
ALUSI:89:29/r9.anchor: وعن عكرمة والضحاك أن ذلك القول عند البعث فقيل النفس بمعنى الذات أيضاً والمراد بالرب هو الله عز وجل

ALUSI:89:29/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:29/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI:89:29/r10.claim: Another analysis takes nafs as the soul and rabb as its owner, the body: the soul returns to its former body, then enters the servants and the abode of reward.
ALUSI:89:29/r10.anchor: وقيل النفس بمعنى الروح والمراد بالرب الصاحب وفسر بالجسد وباقي الآية على حاله

ALUSI:89:29/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:29/r12.speaker: ابن زيد وجماعة
ALUSI:89:29/r12.claim: Ibn Zayd and a group say the address comes at death, with the soul understood as the spirit returning to the sacred realm and then joining the close servants.
ALUSI:89:29/r12.anchor: وقال ابن زيد وجماعة إن ذلك القول عند الموت

ALUSI:89:29/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:29/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI:89:29/r15.claim: On the death-time reading, the soul is pleased with its bliss and pleasing to God; entry among the close servants follows immediately, while entry into the eternal Garden follows at resurrection, though certainty permits the future event to follow by fa.
ALUSI:89:29/r15.anchor: وهذا الدخولان يعقبان الرجوع إلا أن الدخول الأول يعقبه بلا تراخ قبل يوم القيامة والثاني يعقبه بتراخ

ALUSI:89:29/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:29/r16.speaker: author
ALUSI:89:29/r16.claim: Other proposed sequencing allows both commands without delay: entry among the servants may mean joining righteous souls of one’s kind or their bodies, and Garden entry may be temporary enjoyment before the Hour.
ALUSI:89:29/r16.anchor: وجوز أن يكون تعقيب الأمرين بلا تراخ إن أريد بالدخول في العباد الدخول في زمرة المقربين

ALUSI:89:29/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:29/r17.speaker: author
ALUSI:89:29/r17.claim: The temporary-Garden proposal cites a hadith that believers’ souls are in birds’ crops in Paradise and an athar that a believer receives half his promised Garden at death; al-Ālūsī calls the mirror-and-radiance explanation of their gathering rhetorical speculation.
ALUSI:89:29/r17.anchor: ففي الحديث أن أرواح المؤمنين في حواصل طيور في الجنة وفي بعض الآثار إذا مات المؤمن أعطى نصف الجنة

ALUSI:89:29/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:29/r18.speaker: أبو صالح
ALUSI:89:29/r18.claim: Abū Ṣāliḥ says the return is at death, meaning departure from worldly life, while the two entry commands are spoken at resurrection.
ALUSI:89:29/r18.anchor: أخرج ابن جرير وابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم عن أبي صالح أنه قال في الآية

ALUSI:89:29/r19.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:29/r19.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي
ALUSI:89:29/r19.claim: Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb al-Quraẓī places the address after death but before resurrection: the believer sees his Garden home, returns to the body, and awaits questioning by Munkar and Nakīr; no grading is stated.
ALUSI:89:29/r19.anchor: أخرج ابن المنذر عن محمد بن كعب القرظي أنه قال في الآية إن المؤمن إذا مات

ALUSI:89:29/r20.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:29/r20.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
ALUSI:89:29/r20.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam says the soul is given glad tidings of Paradise at three stages: death, resurrection, and the day of gathering.
ALUSI:89:29/r20.anchor: أخرج ابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم عن زيد بن أسلم أنه قال في الآية

ALUSI:89:29/r21.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:29/r21.speaker: author
ALUSI:89:29/r21.claim: An inward reading applies the commands throughout earthly life: turn to God in every matter, join the sincere servants through good works, and enter the Garden potentially; al-Ālūsī says this is not a sound interpretation.
ALUSI:89:29/r21.anchor: وقيل يجوز أن يكون ذلك في سائر أوقات النفس في حياتها الدنيا

ALUSI:89:29/r22.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:29/r22.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI:89:29/r22.claim: A report through Juwaybir from al-Ḍaḥḥāk identifies the occasion with ʿUthmān’s purchase of Biʾr Rūma for public water; al-Ālūsī treats such identifications as examples, not limits on the verse.
ALUSI:89:29/r22.anchor: ابن أبي حاتم من طريق جويبر عن الضحاك عن ابن عبا سأنها نزلت في عثمان بن عفان

ALUSI:89:29/r23.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:29/r23.speaker: author
ALUSI:89:29/r23.claim: Other reported occasions identify the tranquil soul with Ḥamza or with Khubayb ibn ʿAdī, whose face was miraculously turned toward the qibla after his captors faced it toward Medina; these too are examples.
ALUSI:89:29/r23.anchor: وقيل إنها نزلت في حمزة بن عبد المطلب وقيل نزلت في خبيب بن عدي

ALUSI:89:29/r24.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:29/r24.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI:89:29/r24.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās is also reported to identify the soul as the Prophet; al-Ālūsī likewise treats this as an illustrative identification rather than restricting the verse’s general meaning.
ALUSI:89:29/r24.anchor: قول ابن عباس في تلك النفس كما أخرجه عنه ابن مردويه هو النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

ALUSI:89:29/r25.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:29/r25.speaker: author
ALUSI:89:29/r25.claim: Some readings imply that souls existed before bodies in the realm of dominion; al-Ālūsī notes that most theologians, like Plato and his followers, instead hold that souls are created when bodies become ready for them.
ALUSI:89:29/r25.anchor: وجمهور المتكلمين على أنها مخلوقة عند استعداد الأبدان لها وكذا أفلاطون وأصحابه

ALUSI:89:29/r27.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:29/r27.speaker: السادة الصوفية
ALUSI:89:29/r27.claim: Sufi authors see three stations in the passage—tranquil, content, and approved—and explain each in their works.
ALUSI:89:29/r27.anchor: وقالوا إن الآية متضمنة لمراتب ثلاث منها المطمئنة والراضية والمرضية

ALUSI:89:30/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:30/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI:89:30/r2.claim: Entering God’s Garden is the bodily happiness promised to the tranquil soul, prepared for such souls.
ALUSI:89:30/r2.anchor: وادخلي جنتي التي أعددتها لذوي النفوس المطمئنة

ALUSI:89:30/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:30/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI:89:30/r3.claim: The first command signifies spiritual happiness through companionship with the righteous; the second signifies bodily happiness, and the superior spiritual reward is mentioned first, with the Garden completing it.
ALUSI:89:30/r3.anchor: إشارة إلى السعادة الروحانية لكمال استئناس النفس بالجليس الصالح والأمر بدخول الجنة إشارة إلى السعادة الجسمانية

ALUSI:89:30/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:30/r4.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI:89:30/r4.claim: Abu Hayyan explains that dukhūl takes fī with a figurative or nonliteral domain, but usually takes a real container directly.
ALUSI:89:30/r4.anchor: قال أبو حيان لأن المدخول فيه إن كان غير ظرف حقيقي تعدى إليه في الاستعمال بفي

ALUSI:89:30/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:30/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI:89:30/r5.claim: One reading takes ‘return to your Lord’s promise’ as the promised Garden and company of the righteous, spoken after the reckoning; the objection that this implies prior residence is answered by a potential existence in Adam’s loins while he was in the Garden.
ALUSI:89:30/r5.anchor: وقيل المراد ارجعي إلى موعد ربك واستظهر أن المراد بموعده تعالى

ALUSI:89:30/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:30/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI:89:30/r6.claim: The proposed prior existence is compared with reports from ʿAlī and Ibn ʿAbbās that maʿād in 28:85 means Paradise rather than Mecca; this works only if Adam’s Garden was the eschatological Garden, a strongly disputed identification discussed by Ibn al-Qayyim.
ALUSI:89:30/r6.anchor: على ما روى عن أمير المؤمنين علي كرم الله تعالى وجهه وعن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما من أن المراد بالمعاد الجنة دون مكة

ALUSI:89:30/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:30/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI:89:30/r7.claim: Another interpretation makes ‘return to your Lord’s command’ mean return to one of His affairs: His treatment of her without distress, placement in an honored station, or something similar.
ALUSI:89:30/r7.anchor: وقيل المراد ارجعي إلى أمر ربك واستظهر أن المراد بالأمر على ذلك التقدير

ALUSI:89:30/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:30/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI:89:30/r8.claim: A further view understands the return as return to God’s general favor, from the barzakh after death or from the period after resurrection but before judgment.
ALUSI:89:30/r8.anchor: وقيل المراد ارجعي إلى كرامة ربك ويراد جنس كرامته سبحانه

ALUSI:89:30/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:30/r9.speaker: عكرمة والضحاك
ALUSI:89:30/r9.claim: ʿIkrima and al-Ḍaḥḥāk place the address at resurrection; on one analysis nafs means the person, Lord means God, and an implied noun supplies the station to which she returns.
ALUSI:89:30/r9.anchor: وعن عكرمة والضحاك أن ذلك القول عند البعث فقيل النفس بمعنى الذات أيضاً والمراد بالرب هو الله عز وجل

ALUSI:89:30/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:30/r10.speaker: author

BAGHAWI:89:30/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:89:30/r1.speaker: بعض أهل الإشارة
BAGHAWI:89:30/r1.claim: An inward reading addresses the soul attached to worldly life: return to God by leaving it, since return to God means following the path of the afterlife.
BAGHAWI:89:30/r1.anchor: وقال بعض أهل الإشارة : يا أيتها النفس المطمئنة إلى الدنيا ارجعي إلى الله بتركها ،   والرجوع إلى الله هو سلوك سبيل الآخرة .

BAGHAWI:89:30/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:89:30/r2.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
BAGHAWI:89:30/r2.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr reports that at Ibn Abbas's funeral in Taif a strange bird entered his bier and was not seen leaving; these verses were recited at his grave, though the reciter was unknown.
BAGHAWI:89:30/r2.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير : مات ابن عباس بالطائف فشهدت جنازته ،   فجاء طائر لم ير على صورة خلقه فدخل نعشه

BAYDAWI:89:30/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:89:30/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:89:30/r1.claim: The soul may enter Paradise with the righteous servants, or among the proximate whose light reflects upon one another like facing mirrors.
BAYDAWI:89:30/r1.anchor: معهم أو في زمرة المقربين فتستضيء بنورهم فإن الجواهر القدسية كالمرايا المتقابلة

BAYDAWI:89:30/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:89:30/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:89:30/r2.claim: Another interpretation is that the soul returns to the bodies of the servants it left and enters the prepared abode of reward.
BAYDAWI:89:30/r2.anchor: أو ادخلي في أجساد عبادي التي فارقت عنها وادخلي دار ثوابي التي أعدت لك

BAYDAWI:89:30/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:89:30/r3.speaker: رسول الله
BAYDAWI:89:30/r3.claim: The Prophet says that reciting al-Fajr during the ten nights brings forgiveness, and reciting it on other days gives light on Judgment Day.
BAYDAWI:89:30/r3.anchor: عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم من قرأ سورة الفجر في الليالي العشر غفر له

BIQAI:89:30/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:89:30/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI:89:30/r1.claim: God's garden here is the Garden of Eden, the highest of the gardens.
BIQAI:89:30/r1.anchor: أي وهي جنة عدن وهي أعلى الجنان

BIQAI:89:30/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:89:30/r2.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
BIQAI:89:30/r2.claim: Al-Baghawi relates from Saʿid ibn Jubayr that when Ibn ʿAbbas died at al-Taʾif, an extraordinary bird entered his bier and was not seen leaving; at burial this verse was recited by an unknown voice.
BIQAI:89:30/r2.anchor: قال البغوي : قال سعيد بن جبير : مات ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما بالطائف

BIQAI:89:30/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:89:30/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI:89:30/r3.claim: The ending fulfills the opening oath by the dawn: its apparent subject is the inevitable resurrection, without which creation would be vain.
BIQAI:89:30/r3.anchor: على ما هو ظاهر المقسم عليه بالفجر من البعث المحتوم

BIQAI:89:30/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:89:30/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI:89:30/r4.claim: The author praises the Qur'an's meanings, composition, and order as standing at the summit of inimitability, as inaccessible as the Pleiades to a grasping hand.
BIQAI:89:30/r4.anchor: غر في ذروة الإعجاز تركيبه ونظامه

DURR:89:28/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:89:28/r4.speaker: الحسن
DURR:89:28/r4.claim: Hasan says at a believer's death the soul finds rest in God, is pleased with Him and He with it; God takes it, admits it to Paradise, and makes it one of His righteous servants.
DURR:89:28/r4.anchor: عن الحسن رضي الله عنه في قوله : { يا أيتها النفس المطمئنة } الآية ، قال : إن الله إذا أراد قبض عبده المؤمن اطمأنت النفس إليه

DURR:89:28/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:89:28/r5.speaker: أبو صالح
DURR:89:28/r5.claim: Abu Salih locates the soul's return to God at death as it leaves the world; the commands to join God's servants and enter Paradise come on the Day of Resurrection.
DURR:89:28/r5.anchor: عن أبي صالح رضي الله عنه في قوله : { ارجعي إلى ربك } قال : هذا عند الموت رجوعها إلى ربها خروجها من الدنيا

DURR:89:28/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:89:28/r9.speaker: قتادة
DURR:89:28/r9.claim: Qatada says the believer is reassured by God's promise; entering among God's servants means joining the righteous, followed by entry into Paradise.
DURR:89:28/r9.anchor: عن قتادة { يا أيتها النفس المطمئنة } قال : هذا المؤمن اطمأن إلى ما وعد الله { فادخلي في عبادي } قال : ادخلي في الصالحين

DURR:89:28/r14.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:89:28/r14.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
DURR:89:28/r14.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr recounts that an unfamiliar bird entered Ibn Abbas's bier and was never seen leaving; as Ibn Abbas was buried, this passage was recited at the grave edge by an unknown speaker.
DURR:89:28/r14.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير رضي الله عنه قال : مات ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما بالطائف

DURR:89:29/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:89:29/r4.speaker: الحسن
DURR:89:29/r4.claim: Al-Hasan says that when God takes a believer, the soul and God are mutually at ease and satisfied; God then admits it to Paradise among the righteous.
DURR:89:29/r4.anchor: عن الحسن رضي الله عنه في قوله : { يا أيتها النفس المطمئنة } الآية ، قال : إن الله إذا أراد قبض عبده المؤمن

DURR:89:29/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:89:29/r5.speaker: أبو صالح
DURR:89:29/r5.claim: Abu Salih distinguishes the soul's return at death, as it leaves worldly life, from the command at Resurrection to enter God's servants and Paradise.
DURR:89:29/r5.anchor: عن أبي صالح رضي الله عنه في قوله : { ارجعي إلى ربك } قال : هذا عند الموت رجوعها إلى ربها خروجها من الدنيا

DURR:89:29/r14.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:89:29/r14.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
DURR:89:29/r14.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr reports that after Ibn Abbas died at Taif, an extraordinary bird entered his bier and was never seen leaving; after burial someone unknown recited this passage at his grave.
DURR:89:29/r14.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير رضي الله عنه قال : مات ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما بالطائف ،   فجاء طير لم تر عين خلقته

DURR:89:30/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:89:30/r4.speaker: الحسن
DURR:89:30/r4.claim: Al-Hasan says that when God takes a believer, the soul and God are mutually at ease and satisfied; God then admits it to Paradise among the righteous.
DURR:89:30/r4.anchor: عن الحسن رضي الله عنه في قوله : { يا أيتها النفس المطمئنة } الآية ، قال : إن الله إذا أراد قبض عبده المؤمن

DURR:89:30/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:89:30/r5.speaker: أبو صالح
DURR:89:30/r5.claim: Abu Salih distinguishes the soul's return at death, as it leaves worldly life, from the command at Resurrection to enter God's servants and Paradise.
DURR:89:30/r5.anchor: عن أبي صالح رضي الله عنه في قوله : { ارجعي إلى ربك } قال : هذا عند الموت رجوعها إلى ربها خروجها من الدنيا

DURR:89:30/r14.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:89:30/r14.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
DURR:89:30/r14.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr reports that after Ibn Abbas died at Taif, an extraordinary bird entered his bier and was never seen leaving; after burial someone unknown recited this passage at his grave.
DURR:89:30/r14.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير رضي الله عنه قال : مات ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما بالطائف ،   فجاء طير لم تر عين خلقته

IBNASHUR:89:28/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:89:28/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:89:28/r8.claim: The possessive forms ‘My servants’ and ‘My Garden’ shift from third-person reference to first-person speech.

IBNASHUR:89:29/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:89:29/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:89:29/r1.claim: The two commands spell out the preceding general good news; this detail after summary renews the recipients' joy.
IBNASHUR:89:29/r1.anchor: فهو تفصيل بعد الإجمال لتكرير إدخال السرور

IBNASHUR:89:30/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:89:30/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:89:30/r1.claim: The possessive ‘My Garden’ honors Paradise, as does the description of a seat of truth with the Mighty King.
IBNASHUR:89:30/r1.anchor: وإضافة ( جنة ) إلى ضمير الجلالة إضافة تشريف كقوله

IBNASHUR:89:30/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:89:30/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:89:30/r2.claim: This possessive makes the shift to first-person speech especially fitting after ‘your Lord’ was spoken in third person.
IBNASHUR:89:30/r2.anchor: وهذه الإضافة هي مما يزيد الالتفات إلى ضمير التكلُّم حسناً

IBNASHUR:89:30/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:89:30/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:89:30/r3.claim: Repeating ‘enter’ rather than combining the phrases emphasizes entry into the Garden and intensifies the recipients' joy.
IBNASHUR:89:30/r3.anchor: وتكرير فعل { وادخلي } فلم يقل : فادخلي جنتي في عبادي

IBNATIYYA:89:29/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:89:29/r4.speaker: سالم بن عبد الله
IBNATIYYA:89:29/r4.claim: Salim ibn Abd Allah reads “enter among My servants, and enter My garden.”
IBNATIYYA:89:29/r4.anchor: وقرأ سالم بن عبد الله : " فادخلي في عبادي ولجي جنتي "

IBNATIYYA:89:30/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:89:30/r1.speaker: سالم بن عبد الله
IBNATIYYA:89:30/r1.claim: Salim ibn Abd Allah reads “enter among My servants, and enter My garden.”
IBNATIYYA:89:30/r1.anchor: وقرأ سالم بن عبد الله : " فادخلي في عبادي ولجي جنتي "

IBNATIYYA:89:30/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:89:30/r2.speaker: ابن عباس وعكرمة وأبو شيخ والضحاك واليماني ومجاهد وأبو جعفر
IBNATIYYA:89:30/r2.claim: The cited variant reads “enter me among my servant”; the passage says this makes the soul a particular individual, and Abu Shaykh says the spirit enters the body.
IBNATIYYA:89:30/r2.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس ، وعكرمة ، وأبو شيخ ، والضحاك ، واليماني ، ومجاهد ، وأبو جعفر فادخلني في عبدي ) ، فالنفس –على هذا- ليست باسم الجنس

IBNATIYYA:89:30/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:89:30/r3.speaker: أبي بن كعب
IBNATIYYA:89:30/r3.claim: Ubayy's codex expands the address to the assured soul and ends by telling it to return among God's servant.

IBNATIYYA:89:30/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:89:30/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:89:30/r4.claim: The singular “My servant” may be generic, presenting all God's servants as one united body, like the saying that believers are one hand against others.
IBNATIYYA:89:30/r4.anchor: اسم جنس ، جعل عباده كالشيء الواحد دلالة على الالتحام

IBNATIYYA:89:30/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:89:30/r5.speaker: آخرون
IBNATIYYA:89:30/r5.claim: Others place the address at the gathering when people bound for Hell are led away; the souls are addressed with their owners, return is to God's mercy, and the servants are the righteous and God-fearing.
IBNATIYYA:89:30/r5.anchor: وقال آخرون : هذا النداء إنما هو الموقف عندما ينطلق بأهل النار إلى النار ، فنداء النفوس على هذا إنما هو نداء أرباب النفوس مع النفوس

IBNKATHIR:89:27/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:89:27/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:89:27/r4.claim: God calls the soul to join His servants and enter Paradise; this address comes at death and again on Resurrection, as angels announce the believer at death and rising from the grave.
IBNKATHIR:89:27/r4.anchor: وهذا يقال لها عند الاحتضار ، وفي يوم القيامة أيضا ، كما أن الملائكة يبشرون المؤمن عند احتضاره

IBNKATHIR:89:27/r12.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:89:27/r12.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNKATHIR:89:27/r12.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr relates that a strange bird entered Ibn ʿAbbās’s coffin and was not seen leaving; at his burial, someone unknown recited the verse at the grave’s edge.
IBNKATHIR:89:27/r12.anchor: عن سالم الأفطس ، عن سعيد بن جبير قال : مات ابن عباس بالطائف ، فجاء طير لم ير على خلقه

IBNKATHIR:89:27/r13.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:89:27/r13.speaker: قباث بن رزين أبو هاشم
IBNKATHIR:89:27/r13.claim: Qubāth ibn Razīn recounts a captive’s martyrdom in Roman lands: his severed head recited the verse, after which three men who had apostatized returned to Islam.
IBNKATHIR:89:27/r13.anchor: عن قُبَاث بن رزين أبي هاشم قال : أسرت في بلاد الروم ، فجمعنا الملك وعرض علينا دينه

MAWARDI:89:30/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:89:30/r1.speaker: الضحاك
MAWARDI:89:30/r1.claim: The garden can mean God's mercy.

MAWARDI:89:30/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:89:30/r2.speaker: الجمهور
MAWARDI:89:30/r2.claim: Most interpreters take it as the eternal home and dwelling of the righteous.
MAWARDI:89:30/r2.anchor: الثاني : الجنة التي هي دار الخلود ومسكن الأبرار ،   وهو قول الجمهور

MAWARDI:89:30/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:89:30/r3.speaker: أسامة بن زيد
MAWARDI:89:30/r3.claim: Usāma ibn Zayd says the tranquil soul is given glad tidings of Paradise at death, at resurrection, and in Paradise itself.
MAWARDI:89:30/r3.anchor: وقال أسامة بن زيد : بشرت النفس المطمئنة بالجنة عند الموت ،   وعند البعث وفي الجنة .

MAWARDI:89:30/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:89:30/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI:89:30/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that the verse was revealed while Abū Bakr sat with the Prophet; Abū Bakr admired it, and the Prophet said it would be said to him.
MAWARDI:89:30/r4.anchor: فروى ابن عباس أنها نزلت وأبو بكر جالس فقال : يا رسول الله

MAWARDI:89:30/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:89:30/r5.speaker: الضحاك
MAWARDI:89:30/r5.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says it was revealed about ʿUthmān when he endowed the Rūma well in Medina.
MAWARDI:89:30/r5.anchor: الثاني : أنها نزلت في عثمان حين وقف بئر رومة{[3265]} ،   قاله الضحاك

MAWARDI:89:30/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:89:30/r6.speaker: بريدة الأسلمي
MAWARDI:89:30/r6.claim: Burayda al-Aslamī says it was revealed about Ḥamza.
MAWARDI:89:30/r6.anchor: الثالث : أنها نزلت في حمزة ،   قاله بريدة الأسلمي

MAWARDI:89:30/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:89:30/r7.speaker: عكرمة والفراء
MAWARDI:89:30/r7.claim: ʿIkrima and al-Farrāʾ transmit the view that the verse applies generally to all believers.
MAWARDI:89:30/r7.anchor: الرابع : أنها عامة في كل المؤمنين ،   رواه عكرمة والفراء

NASAFI:89:30/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:89:30/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI:89:30/r1.claim: The soul enters God's Garden together with the righteous servants.
NASAFI:89:30/r1.anchor: { وادخلى جَنَّتِى } معهم . وقال أبو عبيدة : أي مع عبادي

QURTUBI:89:30/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:89:30/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI:89:30/r1.claim: The soul is to enter God's Paradise together with His servants.

RAZI:89:27/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:89:27/r3.speaker: القفال
RAZI:89:27/r3.claim: Al-Qaffāl reads the imperative as a report in meaning: when the soul is tranquil, it returns to God and is told to enter among His servants and His garden.
RAZI:89:27/r3.anchor: وقال القفال : هذا وإن كان أمرا في الظاهر لكنه خبر في المعنى

RAZI:89:30/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:89:30/r1.speaker: author
RAZI:89:30/r1.claim: Entering God’s garden here indicates bodily happiness.

RAZI:89:30/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:89:30/r2.speaker: author
RAZI:89:30/r2.claim: The spiritual garden is attained immediately after death, so it follows with fa; bodily Paradise comes only after the great Resurrection, so it follows with wa.
RAZI:89:30/r2.anchor: ولما كانت الجنة الروحانية غير متراخية عن الموت في حق السعداء
